hypothesis: Jerome called the grid updates the bottleneck of the whole method and improving grid BP 'the most valuable next step'. Every experiment runs at N_g = 401 on [-8, 8] (spacing 0.04), a setting chosen for convergence safety and checked only from above (E04, E11: 801 and 1601 change nothing). The exclusive-node time per sequence is 0.52 ms at N_g = 401 and 0.114 ms at 101 (E24x scaling, frozen): 4.6 times faster, which would move BP from 12-18 times slower than the transformer, the GRU and the U-Net (0.03-0.04 ms) to 3-4 times. The accuracy side was never measured, for the oracle or for the learned estimator.
design: Three parts. (a) ORACLE, deterministic, laptop: E32's refinement part, unmodified, with grids (21, 31, 41, 51, 61, 81, 101, 151, 201, 401, 801, 1601) on [-8, 8], reps 0-3, all six phi^4 cells; each grid's relative score error against the (1601, 8) reference. (b) LEARNED, cluster: experiments/e47_coarse_grid.py, E33's fit-and-score path with the BP grid coarsened: E33's own data, noised training views, validation and test bundles and REFERENCE posterior means (the true kernel on the registered 401-point grid), so a risk is the score error of the coarse-grid estimator against the fine-grid truth, discretisation included. Cells T0.3_h1_L32 (base) and T0.3_h0.25_L128 (the finest lattice, a Gaussian bond half as wide); M in (128, 2048); N_g in (51, 101, 201); arms em_pair_quartic and em_tilted_spline; seeds 0-7 (two shards of four: e47b-s0, s4); the comparators are E33's frozen fits at N_g = 401 on the same seeds (test-bundle hashes compared at read time). (c) TIME, cluster, exclusive node: E24's scaling part, unmodified, with grids (41, 51, 61, 81, 101, 151, 201, 401) at B = 512, L = 32, single thread, 9 repeats (e47-time). (d) HEADLINE KERNELS, no refit, laptop: E04's refinement part, unmodified, on the FROZEN E02a headline kernels (the Laplace AR(1) laboratory, M in (32, 2048), C in (1, 8), seeds 0-15) with the ladder (401, 8), (201, 8), (151, 8), (101, 8), (51, 8): each arm's pooled risk against the reference recomputed at that resolution, and the kernels' own 'resolved' flag (does the grid resolve the narrowest component?). This is the AR(1) counterpart of part (b): E23's quadrature table shows that for non-smooth innovations the trapezoid error is NOT super-exponential (the true-kernel BP's median error at 101 nodes is 8e-3 for Laplace and 2e-2 for uniform, against 6e-5 for Student-t and 0 for Gaussian), so the smooth phi^4 result must not be read across to the paper's headline experiments unchecked.

predeclared_predictions.oracle: DESCRIPTIVE, no prediction: the oracle part was SCOUTED before this entry (64 chains, three levels, two cells): the relative score error of the true-kernel BP against the 1601 grid falls from 0.5-0.7 at N_g = 21 (t = 0.05) to 5e-4 at 51 and 1e-11 at 101 (super-exponential, the trapezoid rule on analytic integrands), so thresholds written now would be confirmed trivially. The full table is reported as it is.

outcome.oracle: DESCRIPTIVE. Worst relative score error of the true-kernel BP against (1601, 8), over levels and replicates, at N_g = 101: 1.8e-11 (base cell), 1.0e-11 (h = 0.5), 4.7e-12 (h = 0.25, the finest lattice), 1.3e-12, 3.0e-12, 4.3e-13 (T = 0.5, 1, 2); at N_g = 51: 4.6e-4, 2.4e-4, 7.2e-4, 2.9e-5, 1.7e-5, 1.7e-5; at N_g = 41: 1.6e-3 to 1.5e-2; at 21: 0.51-0.67. Super-exponential in N_g, as scouted. The finest lattice has the largest error at 41 and 51 (1.5e-2, 7.2e-4), but not at 101 (all six are below 2e-11 there).
outcome.P6: CONFIRMED. BP time per sequence (B = 512, L = 32, one thread, exclusive node, median of 9) is 0.053 ms at N_g = 51 (threshold 0.07) and 0.107 ms at 101 (E24x: 0.114; ratio 0.94, inside the 20% band). outcome.P8: CONFIRMED. Headline kernels at N_g = 201: every arm's seed-mean pooled risk within 0.01% of N_g = 401 (worst seed 0.02%).
outcome.P9: CONFIRMED. At N_g = 101: C = 1 within 0.07% (M = 32 and 2048), C = 8 within 0.12% at M = 32 and 2.2% at M = 2048 (worst seed 7.6%). At N_g = 51 the C = 8 M = 2048 kernels move +70% (worst seed +188%); C = 1 moves 2.5-2.8%. At N_g = 151: every arm within 0.08% (worst seed 0.23%).
outcome.P10: FALSIFIED. Only 22% of the C = 8 kernels, pooled over M (7 of 32, the reader's basis), are flagged 'resolved' at N_g = 101 (44% at M = 32, 0% at M = 2048); at 151, 97% pooled (100% at M = 32, 94% at M = 2048); 100% at 201; 0% at 51. The learned mixtures at large M contain components narrower than a 101-point spacing (0.16): the coarse grid is safe for the smooth phi^4 chain at 101 and for the AR(1) headline kernels only from about 151.
outcome.unregistered: Thread count. E24x (the comparator the hypothesis quoted, 0.03-0.04 ms for the transformer, the GRU and the U-Net) ran with 8 BLAS/torch threads on cnode07; part (c) ran with ONE thread, as designed. BP barely uses threads (0.107 vs 0.114 ms at N_g = 101; 0.667 vs 0.524 ms at 401: the matmul is a small share), the networks do: at one thread, per sequence, mlp 0.002, window 0.023, bigru 0.063, unet 0.152, transformer 0.208, tcn 0.216 ms. Per core, BP at N_g = 101 (0.107 ms) is faster than the transformer, the U-Net and the TCN and 1.7 times the bigru; at 151 (0.173 ms) it is within 15% of the U-Net. Not a prediction; the comparison is at matched threads (one) on one node, inference only, B = 512, L = 32.
